deep.reconstruction:
WHAT THE TABLE IS. This page continues, in descending order, a table that runs over several pages. For each prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) between 401 and 881, Gauss lists the cycles (periods) of reduced binary quadratic forms ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant p, in the setting of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, arts. 183–195. Only the outer coefficients |a| are written down.

The principal cycle is identical with the Q_n sequence of the continued fraction of √p. Write ω = ⌊√p⌋ and set P_0 = 0, Q_0 = 1. Then for each n:
- a_n = ⌊(ω + P_n)/Q_n⌋
- P_{n+1} = a_n Q_n − P_n
- Q_{n+1} = (p − P_{n+1}²)/Q_n

Worked example, p = 881 (ω = 29):
- (P,Q) runs (29,40), (11,19), (27,8), (29,5), (26,41), (15,16), (17,37), (20,13), (19,40), (21,11), (23,32), (9,25), (16,25).
- This gives 1,40,19,8,5,41,16,37,13,40,11,32,25,25, exactly as written.

Why the lists stop at a repeated value. For p ≡ 1 (mod 4) prime the period is odd and Q_n is symmetric (Q_n = Q_{l−n}). So there is a central pair Q_k = Q_{k+1}. Gauss stops there and writes '&c' ('the rest is the mirror image'). The existence of this pair is equivalent to the solvability of x² − p y² = −1.

Two-square decomposition (implicit; my addition). Since Q_k Q_{k+1} = p − P_{k+1}², the central pair yields the decomposition p = P_{k+1}² + Q_k², following Legendre's method. Examples:
- 881 = 16² + 25²
- 857 = 4² + 29²
- 821 = 14² + 25²
- 809 = 28² + 5²
- 673 = 12² + 23²
- 661 = 6² + 25²
- 653 = 22² + 13²
- 641 = 4² + 25²
- 593 = 8² + 23²
- 541 = 10² + 21²
- 457 = 4² + 21²
- 433 = 12² + 17²
- 421 = 14² + 15²
- 409 = 20² + 3²
- 733 = 2² + 27²
- 709 = 22² + 15²

Non-principal cycles. Further lines give the other cycles; their number reflects the class number h of properly primitive forms of determinant p, with a class and its inverse sharing one cycle.
- p ≡ 5 (mod 8) with h = 3: a second cycle beginning with 4, or with 3 for 733. Examples are 877, 829, 757, 733, 709, 701, 677, 557.
- Fully checked by me, 757: cycle 4,7,39,12,33,17,21,13,36,11,12,19,28,21,33,4, closing after 15 steps.
- Fully checked by me, 709: cycle 4,21,20,9,25,28,3,11,35,12,29,21,28,15,36,5,45,4.
- p ≡ 1 (mod 8) with h = 3: 761, second cycle 8,17,5,37,16,25,29,8.
- h = 5: 401, cycles 1,1 | 5,8,29,5 | 7,11,16,7. The marginal 0.5 / 1.4 / 2.3 pairs class indices k and h−k of a cyclic group of order 5, which share a cycle.
- h = 7: 577, cycles 1 | 3,16,31,3 | 9,24,23,11,32,9 | 27,8,17,24,19,27. The margin pairs 0–7, 1–6, 2–5, 3–4; the cycles are generated by the form with a = 3 and its powers 3, 9, 27.
- When 4 already occurs in the principal cycle (e.g. 821, 541, 829-type cases excepted), the p ≡ 5 (mod 8) prime has a single cycle.

Purpose. These data feed the recapitulations on the neighbouring pages, which count primes 4n+1 by class number (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11) in each thousand. The page is computational raw material for Gauss's class-number tables for positive determinants.
errors: 661: the principal cycle was first ended prematurely as '…4.9.29.29 &c'. The correct continuation is 29.20.27.15.31.12.25.25 (since (661−9²)/29 = 20). Gauss corrected this by overwriting; the struck '29 &c' is not part of the final sequence. A central pair 29,29 is impossible anyway, as 29² > 661.
457: the line is cut off at the margin without '&c'; the sequence itself (after the reading correction below) is correct.
Overwritten digits at 809 ('35'), 653 ('28'), 593 ('16'), 433 ('13') and 769 ('8') are corrections. In each case the final value agrees with recomputation.

Spot-checked entries all agree with recomputation: 881, 877, 857, 821, 809, 757 (second cycle), 733, 709 (both cycles), 673, 661 (corrected), 653, 641, 593, 541, 433, 421, 409, 677 (second cycle). No other slips found.

results.what: Periods of reduced forms of determinant p (equivalently the Q_n of the continued fraction of √p) for primes 401 ≤ p ≤ 881 with p ≡ 1 mod 4, with the half-period ending at a repeated term.
results.modern_name: Continued fraction expansion of √p / cycles of reduced indefinite binary quadratic forms (Gauss reduction)

results.what: Symmetric odd period with central pair Q_k = Q_{k+1}, giving p = P² + Q² (two-square decomposition) and solvability of x² − p y² = −1.
results.modern_name: Legendre's continued-fraction method for p = a² + b²; negative Pell equation for p ≡ 1 mod 4

results.what: Enumeration of all cycles per determinant, i.e. class numbers h(4p) (1, 3, 5, 7), with the cyclic group structure indicated for 401 (h = 5) and 577 (h = 7) by pairing k with h−k.
results.modern_name: Class numbers of real quadratic orders / class group of forms of discriminant 4p

deep.surprise_reason: These are raw computations behind Gauss's well-known tables of class numbers for positive determinants, published in Werke II from the Nachlass. The method is standard Lagrange/Legendre/Gauss reduction. The data are correct apart from one corrected slip, but nothing here is new.

checkable.asserts: Central pair 25,25 for 881 gives the two-square decomposition
Partial quotients consistent with Gauss's Q-sequence 1,40,19,…,25,25 for 881 (odd period 25)
In the 661 cycle, the value after 29 is 20, not 29 (Gauss's initial slip)
Corrected 661 cycle ends at central pair 25,25
In the 457 cycle, the term after 9 is 29
Second cycle of 757 through the form with a = 4 has neighbours 7 and 33, as written
Two-square decompositions implied by the central pairs of each principal cycle

transcription_corrections: 457: read '…3.32.9.29.8.21.21' — the digit after 9 is 29, not 24 (recomputation forces 29).
661: final reading is '1.36.15.20.11.12.3.44.5.17.33.4.9.29.20.27.15.31.12.25.25 &c'. The '29.29 &c' was overwritten by Gauss and is not a separate second cycle.
769: the two lines form one sequence, 1.40.15.32.17.24.31.3.48.5.8.41.9.16.15.19.27.24.25.25 &c. The second line is a continuation, not a second cycle.
Top-right header '(11)' is the circled folio number. The bottom '37.11.' under 677 is an unexplained side note.
